cues.text: The empty chair
Johan Cruyff was born in Amsterdam, in the Netherlands, in 1947.
His family lived five minutes from the Ajax stadium, and his father, Manus, was an Ajax fan.
On his tenth birthday, Johan joined the Ajax youth team.
Then, on 8 July 1959, when Johan was twelve, his father died of a heart attack.
Lift the paper shutter to see the family photo.
Losing a parent is one of the hardest things that can happen to anyone.
It was a sadness that shaped the rest of his life.
When someone you love dies, it is okay to feel sad. Talk to someone you trust.
A new way for the family
Johan’s mother, Nel, could not keep the family’s vegetable shop going on her own, so she had to give it up.
Instead, she found work at Ajax as a cleaner, cleaning the lockers.
There she met Henk Angel, the club’s caretaker, and later she married him.
Tap three times to follow the family’s new path.
The shop door closes, the club door opens, and the family grows.
Later, Johan worked hard to give his whole family, and his new stepfamily, a safe and secure life.
Families can change shape and still love each other. We get through hard times together.
A second family
A youth coach who lived nearby, Jany van der Veen, had spotted Johan playing and invited him to Ajax.
Johan was small and not yet strong, so the coach Vic Buckingham encouraged him to go to the gym and made sure he ate better food.
Later, the coach Rinus Michels became almost like a father to him, even though they often argued.
Lift the three flaps to meet the people who helped.
With them, Ajax won the European Cup in 1971, 1972 and 1973.
You can find a second family: coaches, teammates and friends who look out for you.
Hurt, then back
In his early years, Johan was often injured or unwell.
At the start of the 1970–71 season he hurt his groin and could not play.
When he came back on 30 October 1970, against PSV, a teammate had his usual number 9 shirt, so he wore number 14.
Pull the lever to turn the shirt from 9 to 14.
He kept number 14 from then on, and it became famous.
By the 1974 World Cup he was back at his best, and his clever turn against Sweden became known as the Cruyff Turn.
A setback is not the end of the story. Rest, heal, and come back in your own way.
So close
At the 1974 World Cup, the Netherlands reached the final against West Germany.
In the very first minute, Johan was fouled, and his teammate Johan Neeskens scored the penalty.
But West Germany came back and won 2–1.
The defeat hurt the whole country for many years.
Flip the score cards and watch the result change.
Even so, Johan was voted the best player of the whole tournament, and football fans everywhere had loved his team’s brave, exciting football.
You are more than one result. You can lose and still be proud of how you played.
Making space for others
Johan smoked cigarettes from when he was a teenager.
In February 1991 he had a heart attack and needed heart surgery.
Afterwards he gave up smoking and helped health campaigns.
In 1997 he started the Johan Cruyff Foundation, to help children who have a harder start and children with special needs.
Unfold the court between the houses.
His foundation has built more than 200 Cruyff Courts in 22 countries, where children of all backgrounds play together.
Johan died of lung cancer in 2016, with his family around him.
Look after your body, and make space for everyone to play.
